The test image shows two tomato stems split/cut longitudinally, revealing internal brown vascular/pith discoloration. Roots are visible and appear brown. This is a stem/root presentation suggesting a vascular wilt disease.

Let me read the part index and start viewing reference images.

The stem is the primary affected part (plus roots visible). Stem candidates: Alternaria_Black_Molds_Stem_Cankers, Anthracnose, Bacterial_Canker_And_Wilt_Of_Tomato, Bacterial_Wilt, Gray_Mold, Late_Blight, Rhizopus_Soft_Rots, Sclerotinia_Timber_Rot, Southern_Bacterial_Wilt, Southern_Blight.

Top suspects given internal brown vascular/pith discoloration on split stems: Southern_Bacterial_Wilt, Sclerotinia_Timber_Rot, Bacterial_Wilt.
Southern_Bacterial_Wilt reference shows longitudinally cut stems with brown pith discoloration throughout — very similar to the test image. Let me check Bacterial_Wilt and Sclerotinia_Timber_Rot.
Bacterial_Wilt reference shows the streaming test (stem in water beaker) — not matching the test image. Let me check Sclerotinia_Timber_Rot and Alternaria next.
Sclerotinia shows white cotton mycelium and sclerotia — not matching. Let me check Alternaria and Southern_Blight.
Alternaria reference is a microscopy image — not matching. Let me check Southern_Blight and Gray_Mold stems.
Southern_Blight shows bleached external stem lesion, not matching the internal brown pith discoloration in the test image. Let me check Gray_Mold and Late_Blight stems.
Gray_Mold reference is microscopy — not matching. Let me check Late_Blight stem and Southern_Bacterial_Wilt root.
Late_Blight shows external dark stem lesion — not matching. Now let me view Southern_Bacterial_Wilt root for my final view.

This is a decisive match. The Southern_Bacterial_Wilt root reference (Bugwood_2.jpg, ID 5473711) shows:
- Dark brown stem base transitioning to green above
- Fibrous brown root system on white background

The test image (ID 5473712) is the consecutive Bugwood image from the same set — showing two stems split longitudinally to reveal internal brown pith discoloration, same white background, same root system. This is unmistakably Southern_Bacterial_Wilt.

The stem reference (Bugwood_13.jpg) also confirmed this with longitudinally cut stems showing brown pith throughout.
